title: Design a Chat System
summary: Design a real-time chat system supporting 1:1 and group messaging.
body:
Design a real-time chat system supporting 1:1 and group messaging.

## Scenario

Design a chat application like WhatsApp or Slack that supports real-time messaging between users.

## Requirements

- 1:1 and group messaging
- Online/offline status indicators
- Message delivery receipts (sent, delivered, read)
- Message history and search
- Support 50M daily active users

## Constraints

- Messages delivered in < 500ms for online users
- Messages must never be lost
- Support offline message queuing
- End-to-end encryption for 1:1 chats

## What a strong answer covers

- WebSocket vs long polling for real-time delivery
- Message storage and fanout strategy
- Presence service design
- Group message delivery optimization
- Handling network partitions

## Reference walkthrough

WebSocket connections through a gateway service. Message queue (Kafka) for reliable delivery. Chat service writes to a message store (Cassandra for write-heavy workload). Fan-out-on-write for small groups, fan-out-on-read for large channels. Presence service using heartbeats with Redis. Push notifications via FCM/APNs for offline users.
keyTakeaways: WebSocket vs long polling for real-time delivery
